t: A single city-state created in 408 BCE by the union of the three old cities of Rhodes: Ialysos, Kamiros and Lindos.
Its skilled navy policed the eastern Mediterranean and protected the grain trade, making it the leading Hellenistic sea power.
Rome’s punishment in 167 BCE broke its economy, and it lost its freedom to Claudius and finally to Vespasian.
dyk: After the Colossus fell in an earthquake, its remains lay where they had fallen for centuries; Pliny the Elder wrote that few people could wrap their arms around its thumb.
ev: Ialysos, Kamiros and Lindos unite to found the city of Rhodes
Rhodes withstands the siege of Demetrius Poliorcetes
Completion of the Colossus of Rhodes by Chares of Lindos
An earthquake ruins the city and topples the Colossus
The Rhodian fleet defeats a Seleucid squadron under Hannibal off Side
The Treaty of Apamea gives Rhodes Lycia and much of Caria
Rome takes Lycia and Caria and makes Delos a free port
Gaius Cassius captures and plunders Rhodes

f.founder: Ialysos, Kamiros and Lindos (synoecism of 408–407 BCE)
